players.product: Power-first greenfield AI data-center campuses on 15-year triple-net leases (River Bend LA for Anthropic; Beacon Point TX) - ex-Bitcoin-mining platform (American Bitcoin affiliate)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 results (CFO): revenue grew 45% to $235.1 million, driven primarily by the compute segment, while cost of revenue grew 24% to $107.8 million; gross margin expanded from 47% to 54%. Q4 2025 revenue grew 179% versus Q4 2024 and gross margin expanded from 36% to 60%. Net loss was $248 million and adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $135.4 million, versus net income of $331.4 million and adjusted EBITDA of $555.7 million in 2024, a swing largely due to a $220 million primarily unrealized mark-to-market loss on the Bitcoin stack.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $235.1 million (+45%); gross margin 47% to 54%; Q4 revenue +179%, gross margin 36% to 60%; net loss $248 million; adjusted EBITDA loss of $135.4 million

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 segments (CFO): power revenue was $23.2 million versus $56.6 million in 2024 (the decline reflects termination of the Ionic Digital managed-services agreement, partly offset by Far North on power market tightness); compute was 'the real growth engine', revenue more than doubling to $202.3 million from $80.7 million, including a full year of steady-state Highrise AI operations which added $7.4 million year-over-year; compute segment margins expanded from 44% to 61%. Digital infrastructure margins improved as Vega entered commercialization and American Bitcoin moved to colocation-based payments.
quarterly_data.figure: power $23.2 million vs $56.6 million; compute $202.3 million vs $80.7 million; Highrise AI added $7.4 million; segment margins 44% to 61%

quarterly_data.signal: River Bend execution (CEO): everything was locked in when the deal was announced - people, contractors, long lead time items, equipment; construction is tracking to plan with Jacobs Engineering and Vertiv, and 'Vertiv is fully cranking on the long lead time items'. The first data center comes online in the beginning of Q2, then a data center every 60 days thereafter; asked how many data halls are in the initial phase, he said 'There are 4 data centers in this data hall' (year not stated on the call). Hut 8 is in active negotiations on the OSA (operations and delivery). 2026 is 'about execution and delivery, full stop.'
quarterly_data.figure: 4 data centers; a data center coming online every 60 days after the first

quarterly_data.signal: River Bend project financing (CEO): the announced target of 85% LTC at SOFR plus 225 was improved to 90% LTC at SOFR plus 240; JPMorgan and Goldman are committed and Hut 8 is pushing aggressively toward closing. The equity portion is already fully funded (including deposits with Vertiv), so closing returns a 'multi-hundred million dollar cash out' and Hut 8 then funds its 10% on an ongoing basis. The CFO called it the lowest cost of capital anyone in the sector has raised to support AI infrastructure.
quarterly_data.figure: 85% LTC at SOFR plus 225 improved to 90% LTC at SOFR plus 240

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and pipeline (CEO): development pipeline of 8.5 gigawatts; of capacity under management, 300 megawatts of power generation sold to TransAlta and 700 megawatts of compute supporting American Bitcoin; capacity under construction is 330 megawatts of utility (River Bend Phase 1); over 1 gigawatt sits in capacity under development being commercialized. On the River Bend 1 gigawatt expansion: 'the power is there. It's not about if, it's about when' - Hut 8 is working with Entergy on delivery timelines, upfront collateral and possibly bringing generation to the campus (which can scale to almost 3,000 acres) to reach the full gigawatt faster. The Corpus Christi site has an approved ERCOT interconnect put in in 2023.
quarterly_data.figure: 8.5 gigawatts pipeline; 330 megawatts River Bend Phase 1; 700 megawatts for American Bitcoin; over 1 gigawatt under development

quarterly_data.signal: Value engineering (CEO): Hut 8 developed 180 kilowatts per rack direct-to-chip cooling at Vega when NVIDIA was only at 120 kilowatts per rack, for $455,000 per megawatt including fit-out; it designs and contract-manufactures parts of the stack (switchgear, PDUs, rack structures) and co-designed the River Bend architecture with Vertiv and Jacobs for supply chain visibility and long lead time risk mitigation.

Highrise AI cloud (CEO): Hut 8 is managing 'a little over 1,100 GPUs' with its own cloud network and software stack (bare metal and multi-tenant), and Highrise can provide financing around the GPU stack in future data-center deals; utilization on the Highrise cloud is 'at record highs'. Management gave no GPU scale-up target.

Demand and power (CEO): 'The demand is still there, demand is still strong'; 'A bigger theme that we're seeing that's real is that power is becoming more constrained' as utilities and transmission operators restudy their queues. Hut 8 probably gets 100 inbounds on sites to review from an M&A perspective. Future counterparties are optimized toward investment grade, managed as portfolio risk allocation.

Deposits, Bitcoin and G&A (CFO/CEO): asked about a deposit for future sites (the analyst's figure), management said the dollars go to land options and malleable long lead time equipment (high to medium voltage breakers, transformers) allocable across campuses. Hut 8 intends to remove Bitcoin exposure from its balance sheet, keeping exposure through its equity in American Bitcoin. FY2025 total G&A was about $122.8 million versus $72.9 million (stock-based comp around $57.8 million versus $20.8 million), reflecting investment in the engineering and development team.
